howto.name: Enter the data to encode
howto.text: Type or paste a URL or plain text, or a contact card (vCard) or WiFi login already written in its standard text format; there is no form that builds them for you. Ordinary text can run to about 2,200 characters.

howto.name: Choose size and format
howto.text: Set the size from 100 to 1,200 pixels (300 by default) and download as a PNG image or a one-page PDF containing the same image. You can also change the code and background colours and add a small centre logo.

howto.name: Download the QR
howto.text: Click Generate QR code and download the result; PNG codes also show a preview. Codes use error correction level M, which tolerates about 15% damage, or level H, about 30%, when you add a centre logo.

faq.a: Yes. Pick any colour for the code and the background, and optionally add a small centre logo as a PNG, JPG or WebP image. Keep a dark code on a light background with strong contrast, and scan the finished code before sharing it.

faq.q: How do I encode a URL with parameters?
faq.a: Just paste the full URL. Special characters are encoded automatically inside the QR.

faq.q: What's the maximum data I can encode?
faq.a: About 2,200 characters of ordinary text, such as a long URL, or about 5,300 digits, at the error correction level M the tool uses. Adding a centre logo switches to level H and roughly halves that. Longer input cannot be encoded.
